To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“A systematic review and taxonomy of 454 criteria related to the evaluation and design of user-facing e-Health products was performed and revealed 11 quality domains (Usability, Visual Design; User Engagement, Content; Behavior Change/Persvassive Design; Influence of Social Presence; Therapeutic Alliance; Classification; Credibility/ Accountability; Privacy/Security), 58 quality criteria concepts, and 134 concepts sub-groups.

1) there are many quality criteria related to the evaluation user-facing eHealth and mHealth programs; 2) these criteria can be grouped into a taxonomy; 3) there is consensus on key quality criteria concepts related to eHealth and mhealth programs, but there is also a large amount of new published criteria, and 4) the taxonomy can be used as a starting point to guide the evaluation of eHealth products.

(1) 11 quality domains were identified; (2) these 11 quality domains are further divided into 58 criteria concepts, and (3) these criteria concepts are further divided into a total of 134 concepts’ groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of user-focussed eHealth products.
the evaluation of user facing eHealth programs and not with the development or design of these programs.
the development of a taxonomy of quality criteria for the evaluation of user facing eHealth programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality criteria related to the evaluation and development of user-facing ehealth programs can be grouped into 11 domains: Usability, visual design, user engagement, content, behavior change/persuasive design, influence of social presence, therapeutic alliance, classification, credibility/accountability, and privacy/security.

the evaluation of user facing eHealth products should consider the 11 quality domains (Usability, Visual Design etc.), the 58 criteria concepts (e.g., Usability, Content, Privacy) and the sub-group concepts (e.g. Usability, Navigation).

the evaluation of user- facing eHealth products should be conducted in a way that considers the following 11 quality domains: usability, visual design, user engagement, content, behavior change/persuasive design, influence of social presence, therapeutic alliance, classification, credibility/accountability, privacy/security.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this review has identified a set of 134 quality criteria concepts and sub-concepts that can be used to guide and evaluate the development of user-facing e- and mHealth programs.
the evaluation of user facing eHealth products has evolved from a technical focus to a more holistic approach, which includes the user experience and the therapeutic alliance.

there are a lot of quality criteria that are being used when evaluating user-facing mHealth and eHeath programs, however, there is still no consensus on which criteria are the most important and which are the most relevant to use when evaluating a specific product.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evaluation of user-focused eHealth products has become more sophisticated in the last few years, and that there are now many more criteria concepts that are being considered by researchers and developers.
the criteria identified and grouped here are the most commonly agreed upon criteria for evaluating user-facing ehealth programs.

a taxonomy of evaluation criteria can be used as an initial checklist for researchers, developers, and practitioners to ensure that they have not overlooked important criteria when designing and/or evaluating their eHealth products.
